([[Bel Aire, Kansas]]) | college = [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] (2021–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 48 | draft_team = [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] | career_start = 2022 | career_end = | years1 = {{nbay|2022|start}}–{{nbay|2023|end}} | team1 = [[Indiana Pacers]] | years2 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022]]–[[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team2 = →[[Indiana Mad Ants|Fort Wayne / Indiana Mad Ants]] | years3 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team3 = [[Long Island Nets]] | years4 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team4 = [[Maine Celtics]] | highlights = * [[Big 12]] All-Freshman Team (2022) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2021]]) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2021) }} '''Kendall Thomas Brown''' (born May 11, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor Bears]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the best [[small forward]]s in the 2021 class. ==High school career== As a sophomore at [[East Ridge High School (Minnesota)|East Ridge High School]] in [[Woodbury, Minnesota]], Brown averaged 17.6 points and led the team to its first state tournament appearance. After the season, he transferred to [[Sunrise Christian Academy]] in [[Bel Aire, Kansas]].{{cite web |last=Paulsen |first=Jim |title=Kendall Brown leaving East Ridge for prep school in Kansas |url=https://www.startribune.com/kendall-brown-leaving-east-ridge-for-prep-school-in-kansas/512798892/ |website=[[Star Tribune]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=July 21, 2019}} Brown was teammates with top recruit [[Kennedy Chandler]]. As a senior, he helped his team reach the [[GEICO]] Nationals title game.{{cite web |last=Eldridge |first=Taylor |title='The little engine that could': Sunrise proves it belongs with national hoops powers |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/varsity-kansas/varsity-basketball/article250414321.html |website=[[The Wichita Eagle]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=April 3, 2021}} He was named to the [[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]] rosters.{{cite web |last=Fuller |first=Marcus |title=Five-star homegrown hoops talent Kendall Brown on young athletes giving back: "We have to use the platform we have." |url=https://www.startribune.com/five-star-homegrown-hoops-talent-kendall-brown-on-young-athletes-giving-back-we-have-to-use-the-platform-we-have/571130782/ |website=[[Star Tribune]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=June 9, 2020}}{{cite web |last=James |first=Ryan |title=Kendall Brown had a 5-Star Season at Sunrise Christian |url=https://247sports.com/college/minnesota/LongFormArticle/Minnesota-Basketball-Recruiting-5-Star-Kendall-Brown-had-a-5-Star-Season-at-Sunrise-Christian-146836944/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=May 5, 2020}} ===Recruiting=== Brown was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the best [[small forward]]s in the 2021 class. On July 20, 2020, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] over offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], among others.{{cite web |last=Bedore |first=Gary |title=Kendall Brown, No. 12-ranked player in Class of 2021, picks Baylor over KU, others |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article244352267.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=July 20, 2020}} Brown is the highest-ranked recruit to come to Baylor since [[Isaiah Austin]] in 2012.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |last2=Biancardi |first2=Paul |authorlink2=Paul Biancardi |title=5-star player Brown of Kansas commits to Baylor |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29503107 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |date=July 20, 2020}} He said that since he came from a Christian high school, he liked the fact that Baylor was a Christian university.{{cite web |last=Jordan |first=Jason |title=Elite 2021 Wing Kendall Brown Commits to Baylor |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/kendall-brown-baylor-2021-sunrise-christian-academy |website=SI All-American |date=July 20, 2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Preseason [[Big 12 Conference]] Freshman of the Year.{{cite web |date=October 13, 2021 |title=Big 12 Unveils 2021-22 Men's Basketball Preseason Awards |url=https://big12sports.com/news/2021/10/12/big-12-unveils-2021-22-mens-basketball-preseason-awards.aspx |accessdate=March 30, 2022 |website=big12sports.com}} In his college debut, Brown scored 13 points in a 87–60 victory over [[2021–22 Incarnate Word Cardinals men's basketball team|Incarnate Word]]. He earned Big 12 Newcomer of the Week honors twice (December 20 and March 7).{{cite web|title=MBB Pair Pick up Big 12 Weekly Awards|url=https://baylorbears.com/news/2022/3/7/mens-basketball-mbb-pair-pick-up-big-12-weekly-awards.aspx|date=March 7, 2022|accessdate=March 30, 2022}} As a freshman, Brown averaged 9.7 points and 4.9 rebounds per game. At the end of the season, he was named to the Big 12 All-Freshman Team.{{cite web|title=Men's Basketball All-Big 12 Awards Announced|url=https://big12sports.com/documents/2022/3/6//All_Big_12_Release_21_22_.pdf|date=March 6, 2022|accessdate=March 30, 2022}} On March 30, 2022, Brown declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |date=March 30, 2022 |title=Baylor guard Kendall Brown, potential first-round pick, declares for NBA Draft |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3500935/2022/03/30/baylor-guard-kendall-brown-potential-first-round-pick-declares-for-nba-draft/ |access-date=March 30, 2022 |website=theathletic.com}} ==Professional career== ===Indiana Pacers (2022–2024)=== Brown was selected with the 48th overall pick in the [[2022 NBA draft]] by his hometown team, the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. On June 23, 2022, the Timberwolves traded his draft rights to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in exchange for cash considerations and a 2026 second-round pick.{{cite web|first=Taylor|last=Nardinger|title=Timberwolves Acquire Future Pick and Cash Considerations from Indiana|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-acquire-future-pick-and-cash-considerations-from-indiana|website=NBA.com|date=June 24, 2022|access-date=June 27, 2022}} On September 16, Brown signed a two-way contract with the Pacers.{{cite web|title=Pacers Announce Signings|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-announce-signings|website=NBA.com|date=September 16, 2022|access-date=September 16, 2022}} On February 27, 2023, he underwent surgery to address a tibia stress fracture in his right leg and was ruled out indefinitely by the Pacers.{{cite web|title=Kendall Brown Medical Update - Feb. 27, 2023|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/kendall-brown-medical-update-feb-27-2023|website=NBA.com|date=February 27, 2023|access-date=March 16, 2023}} On July 25, 2023, Brown signed another two-way contract with the Pacers{{cite web|title=Pacers Sign Kendall Brown to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-kendall-brown-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 25, 2023|access-date=July 26, 2023}} and on March 4, 2024, he signed a multi-year contract.{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers Sign Kendall Brown|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-sign-kendall-brown|website=NBA.com|date=March 4, 2024|access-date=March 4, 2024}} On October 15, Brown was waived.{{cite web|title=Pacers Roster Transactions|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-roster-transactions|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2024|access-date=October 15, 2024}} ===Long Island Nets (2024–2025)=== On October 27, 2024, Brown joined the [[Long Island Nets]],{{cite tweet|author=Long Island Nets|title=Our official training camp roster 🔥 #StrongIsland 💪|number=1850674269581197342|user=LongIslandNets|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 28, 2024}} and on February 25, 2025, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{Cite web |date=2025-02-25 |title=Nets Signing Kendall Brown To Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/nets_signing_kendall_brown_to_two_way_contract/s1_17038_41816695 |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=Yardbarker |language=en}} He did not appear for Brooklyn before he was waived on March 4.{{Cite web|title=Nets sign Tyson Etienne to a two-way deal, waive Kendall Brown|url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2025/03/05/nets-sign-tyson-etienne-to-a-two-way-deal-waive-kendall-brown/|access-date=March 5, 2025|website=nydailynews.com|language=en}} ===Maine Celtics (2025–2026)=== Brown joined the [[Boston Celtics]] summer league team for the [[2025 NBA Summer League]]. He was later cut alongside [[Jalen Bridges]] and [[Wendell Moore Jr.]] on October 16, 2025.{{Cite web|title=Report: Boston Celtics cut Jalen Bridges, Kendall Brown, and Wendell Moore|url=https://celticswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/celtics/2025/10/17/report-celtics-cut-jalen-bridges-kendall-brown-and-wendell-moore/86747646007/|access-date=October 23, 2025|website=celticswire.usatoday.com|language=en}} In November 2025, he joined the Celtics' [[NBA G League]] affiliates, the [[Maine Celtics]], ahead of the G League season.{{Cite web |title=Maine Celtics Announce Opening Night Roster |url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/roster-announced-110625 |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=Maine Celtics |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player
